title: Necessity 2: должен / должна / должны (agreement)
description: Должен ('must, obliged') is personal: the subject stays NOMINATIVE and должен agrees with it in gender and number (должен / должна / должно / должны), plus an infinitive.
descriptionRussian: Должен («обязан») — личное слово: подлежащее стоит в ИМЕНИТЕЛЬНОМ падеже, а должен согласуется с ним в роде и числе (должен / должна / должно / должны) плюс инфинитив.
intro: The other way to say you must, and it works in exactly the opposite way. Here you are the subject after all, in the nominative, and the word for 'must' agrees with you the way an adjective would. So a man and a woman say it differently. Two constructions, opposite grammar, similar meaning: keeping them apart is most of the difficulty.
rules: Должен means 'must / be obliged to.' It is PERSONAL: the subject stays nominative (я, Антон, мы), unlike надо/нужно.
Должен agrees with the subject like a short adjective: должен (masc), должна (fem), должно (neut, rare), должны (plural).
The construction is: nominative subject + должен/должна/должны + infinitive. Антон должен работать. Лена должна позвонить.
Contrast with Lesson 1: надо takes the DATIVE and never changes (мне надо); должен takes the NOMINATIVE and agrees (я должен / я должна). Do not mix them.
Pick the ending by the subject's gender and number, not by the speaker: a woman says я должна, a man says я должен, a group says мы должны.
examples: Антон должен работать. (Anton must work.) masculine subject → должен.
Лена должна позвонить врачу. (Lena must call the doctor.) feminine subject → должна.
Мы должны купить билеты. (We must buy tickets.) plural subject → должны.
Я должна отдохнуть. (I must rest.) a woman speaking → должна.
Они должны встать рано. (They have to get up early.) plural → должны.
Ты должен подождать. (You must wait.) masculine 'ты' → должен.

tables.title: должен agrees with the subject (nominative + infinitive)

items.hint: Антон is masculine and singular. Match the ending to the subject.
items.explanation: Должен agrees with the subject like an adjective. Антон is masculine singular, so the form is должен. Антон должен работать.

items.hint: Лена is feminine. Which ending matches a feminine subject?
items.explanation: Лена is feminine singular, so должен takes the feminine ending: должна. Лена должна позвонить врачу. Врачу is dative because звонить takes the dative (from the Dative track).

items.hint: Мы is plural. The plural form ends in -ы.
items.explanation: Мы is plural, so the agreeing form is должны. Мы должны купить билеты. The plural form is the same for мы, вы, and они.

items.hint: The form follows the speaker's gender, not the word 'я'. A woman is feminine.
items.explanation: Должен agrees with the real subject. When a woman says 'я,' the subject is feminine singular, so she uses должна: Я должна отдохнуть. A man would say Я должен отдохнуть.

items.promptEnglish: They have to get up early.
items.explanation: Они is plural, so the form is должны: Они должны встать рано. Plural overrides gender; должны covers groups of any gender.

items.hint: Careful: this sentence uses надо, not должен. Which case does надо take?
items.explanation: This item mixes the two machines to keep them straight. The word here is надо, which is impersonal and takes the DATIVE: тебе. Тебе надо подождать. If the sentence had used должен, it would be «Ты должен подождать» with the nominative ты.

blanks: Маша и Лена _____ купить билеты. (Masha and Lena must buy tickets.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Two people joined by 'и' make a plural subject, so должен takes the plural form должны, regardless of the women's gender. Маша и Лена должны купить билеты.

errorCorrection.explanation: Должен agrees with its subject like a short adjective. Письмо is neuter singular, so the neuter form должно is required: Письмо должно прийти.

Должен is personal and takes a NOMINATIVE subject, not the dative: the «мне должен» blend mixes the two machines. Only надо/нужно take the dative (мне надо); with должен the subject stays nominative: Я должен работать. Use Мне надо работать or Я должен работать, never «мне должен».
Они is plural, so должен takes the plural form должны, not the feminine singular должна. Plural overrides gender. Correct: Они должны подождать.

Должен agrees with its subject, and письмо is neuter, so the form is должно. The neuter должно is less frequent but appears with neuter subjects like письмо or задание. Correct: Письмо должно прийти завтра.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон и Маша должна купить билеты.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton and Masha must buy tickets.
errorCorrection.explanation: Two subjects joined by и form a plural subject, so должен takes the plural должны regardless of each person's gender. Correct: Антон и Маша должны купить билеты.

Должен agrees with its subject, and Антон is masculine singular, so the masculine form должен is required. Choosing должна here would wrongly treat a masculine subject as feminine. Correct: Антон должен позвонить родителям.

minimalPairs.explanation: Должен agrees with its subject. Лена is feminine, so the feminine form должна is correct. Должен would only fit a masculine subject like Антон.
Антон is masculine SINGULAR, so the singular masculine form должен is correct. Должны is plural and would need a plural subject like 'Антон и Лена'.

reviewVocab.definition: must, be obliged to. Personal: the subject is nominative and должен agrees in gender and number (masc должен, fem должна, plural должны), plus an infinitive.
reviewVocab.example: Антон должен работать. Лена должна позвонить. Мы должны подождать.

reviewVocab.definition: two opposite machines for 'I have to': должен takes a nominative subject and agrees (я должен / я должна); надо takes a dative person and never changes (мне надо). Do not mix: «мне должен» and «я надо» are both wrong.
reviewVocab.example: Я должна работать. = Мне надо работать.

reviewVocab.definition: the nominative case, the plain subject form (я, ты, Антон, мы). Должен keeps the subject in the nominative, unlike надо.
